column2: At Christmas and New Year at Camelot, a giant green knight rides in holding a holly branch and an axe and challenges any knight to a game.
A knight may strike the Green Knight one blow with the axe, then must receive a return blow in a year and a day at the Green Chapel.
Gawain humbly asks to take it in place of King Arthur and beheads the knight, who picks up his own head and tells Gawain to find him in a year.
The five-pointed star on Gawain's shield, an endless knot of "five fives" that stands for his perfect truth, faith, and virtue.
Gawain's horse, which carries him through the wild winter journey to find the Green Chapel.
The lord of the castle who hosts Gawain, proposes the exchange game, and turns out to be the Green Knight himself (Bertilak de Hautdesert).
Bertilak's beautiful wife, who visits Gawain in bed three mornings to tempt him, sent by Bertilak as a test.
Each of three days Bertilak hunts while Gawain rests, and they trade whatever each has won at the end of the day.
Bertilak hunts a deer on day one, a boar on day two, and a fox on day three.
The lady gives Gawain one kiss, then two, then three kisses and the green girdle, and he hands over the kisses but hides the girdle.

column1: 11. The obligations Gawain is caught between
column2: Courtesy to the lady, loyalty to his host Bertilak, and his Christian chastity, which he cannot all satisfy at once.

column1: 12. What the girdle is supposed to do
column2: The lady says whoever wears the green belt cannot be killed, so Gawain keeps it to save his life at the Green Chapel.

column1: 13. What the girdle comes to mean
column2: Gawain wears it as a badge of his sin, cowardice and covetousness, and Arthur's court adopts it as a sash of honor.

column1: 14. The three swings at the Green Chapel
column2: First Gawain flinches and the knight stops, second the knight holds back on purpose, and third he nicks Gawain's neck.
They match the three days: two misses for the two days Gawain honestly traded his kisses, and a nick for the third day when he hid the girdle.
Gawain's aunt and Arthur's half-sister, a sorceress taught by Merlin, who sent the Green Knight to test the Round Table's pride and frighten Guinevere.

column1: 17. How Gawain feels about his failure
column2: Ashamed and angry: he calls the girdle the symbol of his cowardice and covetousness and vows to wear it for life.
The court laughs kindly and every knight agrees to wear a green sash in Gawain's honor.
Gawain is the most faultless knight on earth, a pearl beside white peas, but he lacked loyalty only because he loved his life.
